newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S EDILSON HITS TWO IN KASHIMA UPSET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S EDILSON HITS TWO IN KASHIMA UPSET.

text.p: Brazilian Edilson scored twice as Kashiwa stunned Kashima 4-0 on Sunday to inflict the first defeat of the season on the defending J-League champions.
Defender Shigenori Hagimura opened the scoring against the run of play in the 41st minute when he headed home a corner kick from Nozomu Kato for the first goal of his professional career.
Edilson broke free from an unusually disorganised Kashima defence to make it 2-0 eight minutes into the second half and fellow Brazilian Jamelli added a third in the 58th minute.
One minute later, Edilson knocked home his second through the legs of Kashima goalkeeper Masaaki Furukawa.

The shock defeat ended the Antlers' four-match unbeaten run and moved them down from top spot to fourth place on goal difference, level on 12 points with four other teams at the top of the table after six rounds of the first-stage league competition.

Taking over in top position are Gamba Osaka whose Yugoslav midfielder Nebojsa Krupnikovic and Masanobu Matsunami found the net in the first six minutes after the interval as they defeated cross town rivals Cerezo Osaka 2-0.
With Cameroon forward Patrick Mboma back in their line-up following World Cup duty, Gamba dominated for much of the game for a deserved victory.
A 55th minute header by Japanese international Takuya Takagi helped Hiroshima beat Kyoto 1-0 to be in fifth place, also on 12 points.
Welsh defender Mark Bowen scored a 67th minute winner as Shimizu beat Ichihara 2-1 at home, while Urawa downed hosts Kobe 2-0 on first-half goals by Masayuki Okano and Hiromitsu Isogai.
Brazilian Magrao's goal two minutes into extra time helped Kawasaki edge Fukuoka 2-1 away from home.
